idea: Simple ways to protect plumbing during renovation
title: Protect Open Drains During Renovation
description: During bathroom or kitchen renovations, exposed drain pipes are extremely vulnerable to site debris. Tile grout, mortar slurry, and plaster frequently get washed into open stub-outs during daily cleanup. Unlike organic clogs, cement-based materials quickly settle in P-traps and horizontal branch lines, setting hard underwater and creating dense obstructions that standard drain snakes cannot easily clear. Stuffing a rag into the pipe is a common mistake because liquid slurry seeps right through it. Installing an expanding mechanical test plug or a temporary plastic cap provides a reliable seal until final fixture trim-out.
image_prompt: A professional vertical 9:16 photograph of a white PVC drain pipe stub-out protruding vertically from a concrete subfloor during a bathroom renovation. The top of the open PVC pipe is sealed tightly with a heavy-duty mechanical expansion test plug featuring a black rubber ring and a metal wing-nut handle. On the unfinished concrete floor around the pipe base are clear traces of grey tile mortar, dust, and plaster, visually highlighting the protection provided by the plug. Bright daylight coming from an off-camera window illuminates the scene clearly. The main plumbing component is positioned in the center-lower frame with clean space above for overlay integration. Realistic textures, physically accurate DWV pipe dimensions, neutral clean environment, photorealistic detailing, no text, no logos, no watermarks, no fake branding.
visual_story: The visual focuses on an open drain stub-out sitting in the middle of an active masonry work area. The viewer immediately notices the mechanical test plug securely closing off the top of the white PVC pipe while tile mortar and dust cover the surrounding floor. This visually proves how a temporary mechanical seal prevents wet cement slurry and heavy dust from falling directly into the drainage line.

on_image_text.explanation: Tile grout and plaster sink into drain traps and harden underwater during renovation work.
on_image_text.takeaway: Seal open drain stub-outs with test plugs before tiling or plastering begins.
